title: A1: deep learning identifies an antibiotic candidate against gonorrhea
summary: A screen of about six million compounds found candidates active against resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. A1 reduced bacteria in animal models, and proteomics, genetics, and biochemistry confirmed its target, alanine racemase. These are preclinical results, published in Science Translational Medicine.

evidence.tested: Phenotypic screen of 38,650 molecules trained a graph neural network, which screened about 6 million compounds; 213 were validated experimentally, 83 inhibited growth. Two hits were tested in vitro against multidrug-resistant strains, by proteomics (alanine racemase target), in a vagina-on-a-chip model and in a mouse vaginal infection model.
evidence.unknown: Not reported (the abstract describes the in vivo and organ-chip results as showing only early promise).
evidence.ai_role: A graph neural network trained on phenotypic screening data, used to virtually screen the compound library before experimental validation.
